indian.headline: Markets end mixed as closing auction recovery offsets early weakness; rupee hits two-month low.
indian.lead: Markets end mixed as closing auction recovery offsets early weakness; rupee hits two-month low.
indian.brief: Sensex fell 0.16% and Nifty 50 dropped 0.34%, but Bank Nifty rose 0.24% as the closing auction session sparked a late-session rally.
indian.narrative:
Indian indices snapped a three-session losing streak on 11 September, though the day remained mixed overall. The closing auction session (CAS)—a new mechanism introduced to improve price discovery at market close—delivered a sharp recovery in the final hour, lifting Sensex by 138 points (0.19%) to 74,903 and Nifty 50 by 46 points (0.2%) to 23,478. Banking stocks led gains with a +0.2% move, while IT held steady at +0.1% and pharma dipped 0.1%, showing rotation among sectors.

Beyond equities, the rupee weakened sharply, tumbling 37 paise to 95.44 per dollar—its worst day in two months—as rising oil prices tied to geopolitical tensions in the West Asia and strong US dollar demand pressured the currency. SEBI confirmed the closing auction session will remain despite early liquidity concerns and is tweaking derivative pricing rules to ease transition. Meanwhile, the IPO calendar heats up with NSE's own listing (₹1,700–₹1,785) opening 17–21 September, while SS Retail readies a ₹500 crore raise at ₹403–₹424 per share.

tiles.label: Global cues
tiles.sub: US-Iran tensions elevate oil; Trump says war won't end before November elections.

tiles.label: FII activity
tiles.sub: No fresh data on net flows; rupee weakness typically signals outflow pressure.

tiles.label: Crude oil
tiles.sub: West Asia geopolitical tensions keep prices elevated; rupee weakness amplifies import costs.

indian.watch: NSE IPO opens 17 September; track market appetite for exchange stock amid volatility and rupee stress.

us.headline: US markets fell as Fed rate hike odds jumped to 70% amid oil surge and inflation fears.
us.lead: US markets fell as Fed rate hike odds jumped to 70% amid oil surge and inflation fears.
us.brief: S&P 500 dropped 0.58%, Nasdaq fell 0.65%, and Dow slid 0.60% as Tech stocks led losses with a 1.4% decline.
us.narrative:
US markets closed lower on 11 September as inflation concerns and geopolitical tensions pushed interest rate hike expectations sharply higher. Oil prices jumped above $107 per barrel following Houthi seizure of Yemen's Mokha port and Middle East escalation, triggering a global bond selloff. Wholesale prices rose 0.4% in August as expected, but annual inflation remained elevated at 5.4%—far above the Federal Reserve's 2% target. Markets now price a 70% probability of a Fed rate hike next week, rattling investors who fear higher borrowing costs ahead.

Tech stocks bore the brunt of selling, dropping 1.4%, while Financials and Energy also retreated 0.3% and 0.6% respectively. Healthcare declined 0.6%. However, not all earnings disappointed: Oracle beat expectations with cloud infrastructure revenue more than doubling to $7.4 billion on AI data center demand. Separately, investors are actively buying hedges against market volatility as US midterm elections and geopolitical risks loom. In other news, Apple launched its first foldable iPhone at £1,999, and Chinese AI chipmaker Enflame soared 206% on its Shanghai debut, underlining persistent appetite for AI-related plays despite today's broader selloff.

tiles.label: Big mover
tiles.sub: Largest sectoral loser; Oracle a bright spot with cloud revenue doubling.

tiles.label: Key data
tiles.sub: Oil above $107/bbl and August wholesale inflation at 5.4% year-on-year fuel rate hike bets.

tiles.label: Backdrop
tiles.sub: Geopolitical tensions, inflation persistence, and higher borrowing cost fears dominate sentiment.

us.watch: Fed's Wednesday decision on rates and oil price action as Middle East tensions remain the key flashpoint.
